```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

df = pd.read_csv("wdi.csv")

# keep 5 indicators for the dashboard
cols = [
  "country",
  "gdp_per_capita",
  "life_expectancy",
  "inflation_rate",
  "unemployment_rate",
  "exports_gdp_share"
]
dash = df[cols].dropna()

labels = {
  "gdp_per_capita": "GDP per capita (current US$)",
  "life_expectancy": "Life expectancy (years)",
  "inflation_rate": "Inflation rate (annual %)",
  "unemployment_rate": "Unemployment rate (%)",
  "exports_gdp_share": "Exports (% of GDP)"
}
vars_list = ["gdp_per_capita", "life_expectancy", "inflation_rate", "unemployment_rate", "exports_gdp_share"]
```

## Scatter Explorer
This interactive scatter plot allows you to change the X and Y variables using dropdown menus.

```{python}
# default axes
x0 = "gdp_per_capita"
y0 = "life_expectancy"

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=dash[x0],
        y=dash[y0],
        mode="markers",
        text=dash["country"],
        hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>X=%{x}<br>Y=%{y}<extra></extra>"
    )
)

# build dropdowns for x and y
x_buttons = []
for v in vars_list:
    x_buttons.append(dict(
        label=labels[v],
        method="update",
        args=[{"x": [dash[v]]},
              {"xaxis": {"title": labels[v]}}]
    ))

y_buttons = []
for v in vars_list:
    y_buttons.append(dict(
        label=labels[v],
        method="update",
        args=[{"y": [dash[v]]},
              {"yaxis": {"title": labels[v]}}]
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Interactive Scatter Plot (WDI 2022)",
    xaxis_title=labels[x0],
    yaxis_title=labels[y0],
    updatemenus=[
        dict(buttons=x_buttons, direction="down", x=0.02, y=1.15, xanchor="left", yanchor="top", showactive=True),
        dict(buttons=y_buttons, direction="down", x=0.52, y=1.15, xanchor="left", yanchor="top", showactive=True),
    ],
    annotations=[
        dict(text="X variable:", x=0.02, y=1.22, xref="paper", yref="paper", showarrow=False),
        dict(text="Y variable:", x=0.52, y=1.22, xref="paper", yref="paper", showarrow=False),
    ],
    height=600
)

fig
```

## Top 10 Explorer
This bar chart is interactive: you can hover for values and zoom.

```{python}
import plotly.express as px

top10 = dash.sort_values("gdp_per_capita", ascending=False).head(10)
fig2 = px.bar(top10, x="country", y="gdp_per_capita", title="Top 10 Countries by GDP per Capita (WDI 2022)")
fig2.update_layout(xaxis_title="Country", yaxis_title=labels["gdp_per_capita"])
fig2
```
